title: What backup plan should a school or nursery ask its caterer for?
body_html:
A school or nursery should ask its caterer for a written backup plan covering a late delivery, an absent cook, a wrong dietary tray and a sudden change in numbers. The plan matters most on the day something goes wrong, when staff have minutes, not hours. If you are comparing providers, start with institutional catering in Dubai and use this page as your question list.

Why ask before you sign

Children's meals are fixed in the timetable. A late tray affects lessons, rest times and parents' expectations, and a wrong dietary tray is a safety matter, not an inconvenience. A caterer who has thought about these cases will answer quickly. One who has not will give a general reassurance instead.

This page lists questions to ask. It does not state requirements. Check the current rules that apply to your school or nursery with the relevant Dubai authority; the school food rules guide is a starting point.

Risks and the questions to ask

RiskAsk the catererA clear answer includes
Late deliveryWho do we call, and what is the fallback meal?A named contact, a decision time and a simpler backup menu
Cook or driver absentWho covers, and is the cover briefed on our dietary list?A named cover process, not a general promise
Wrong or missing dietary trayHow are trays labelled, checked and handed over?A labelling and sign-off step before the meal is served
Equipment failureWhat happens if hot-holding or transport fails?An alternative route and what the school is told
Ingredient changeHow are we told, and when?Written notice before the meal, with allergen details
Sudden change in numbersWhat is the cut-off, and what happens after it?A stated deadline and a way to add or remove meals

Checklist for administrators

  1. Ask for the plan in writing and keep it with the meal agreement.
  2. Name your own contact for deliveries and one back-up person at school.
  3. Keep a simple fallback for the first day, such as a decision time after which you tell parents.
  4. Check the dietary list system. Ask how allergies and halal requirements are recorded, and who confirms each tray.
  5. Run one test day to see how the plan works when the caterer's team is new to your site.
  6. Review after the first month and note any missed deliveries or tray errors.

A worked example (hypothetical)

A nursery lunch is due at 11:30. By 11:15 the delivery has not arrived. The nursery calls the named contact, who confirms a delay and offers the agreed backup menu. The manager tells staff by 11:20 and parents later receive a short note. Because the plan names a decision time and a contact, nobody has to improvise. This illustrates the table; it is not a record of a real event.

Related reading

For the wider choice between meals and packed lunches, read nursery meals versus packed lunches, and for allergy-aware planning see nut-free and halal nursery meals. Medical or allergy questions about individual children belong with the child's own qualified professional.

Next step

Send the table to every caterer you are comparing and ask for written answers. To discuss meals for your school or nursery, see the institutional catering page.
